title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Google Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers Google Cloud (IAM, API Keys, Cloud Storage). Covers Google Cloud project/org credentials; org policy constraints and VPC Service Controls need an organization resource; Workspace user OAuth and domain-wide delegation are in the separate `google` platform.

controls.name: constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension
controls.what: Lists SAs allowed to mint tokens longer than 1 hour (up to 12 hours).

controls.name: Service Account Token Creator role
controls.what: Only principals granted this role on an SA can mint its short-lived tokens.
controls.setting: IAM policy on the service account

controls.name: Disable service account (serviceAccounts.disable)
controls.what: Immediately disables the SA, which is the documented way to cut off already-issued short-lived tokens.

controls.name: VPC Service Controls
controls.what: Service perimeters with ingress rules limit API access by network origin and identity, even with stolen credentials.

no_control.what: Issued short-lived tokens cannot be revoked individually; only disabling/deleting the SA cuts them off.

controls_unknown: Whether existing keys created before iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours was set get an expiry (docs say 'newly created').
Whether API keys support an expiry setting.
Which audit field identifies the API key or HMAC access ID used on a data-plane request.
Whether GetKeyString/lookupKey calls are logged for keys.lookupKey.
Plan/pricing for VPC Service Controls (needs organization).

auth_paths.name: Short-lived service account credentials (service account impersonation)

authentication.summary: A principal with the Service Account Token Creator role calls the IAM Credentials API (generateAccessToken, generateIdToken, signJwt) to mint a short-lived token for a service account.

federation.details: The caller authenticates first (user, SA or federated identity), so the caller's own login controls apply at minting time. The minted SA token is then used without user CAA checks.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only via VPC Service Controls perimeters on supported services.

renewal.summary: Caller mints a new token while it still holds the Token Creator permission.

administration.summary: Control who holds roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on each SA. Issued tokens cannot be revoked one by one; disable or delete the SA.

offboard.details: The token is issued for a service account, not a user.

expiry.ui: Organization policies > constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension > Manage policy (list SAs allowed up to 12h)

usage.ui: Enable Data Access (Admin Read) for IAM Service Account Credentials API under IAM & Admin > Audit Logs; then Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="iamcredentials.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="GenerateAccessToken"

reads.ui: Enable Data Read for Cloud Storage (IAM & Admin > Audit Logs); Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="storage.googleapis.com" and protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=SA_EMAIL

kill.ui: IAM & Admin > Service accounts > (SA) > Service account status > Disable service account; remove Token Creator grants on the SA
kill.cli: gcloud iam service-accounts disable SA_EMAIL; gcloud iam service-accounts remove-iam-policy-binding SA_EMAIL --member=PRINCIPAL --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator

token_format.notes: OAuth 2.0 access token or OIDC ID token; not documented as prefixed.

log_sources.name: IAM Data Access audit logs (iamcredentials.googleapis.com)
log_sources.notes: Must be enabled; records each token mint.

credential_id_fields.notes: SA the token was minted for

anomaly_cues: New principal minting tokens for a privileged SA

containment.steps: Remove Token Creator bindings; disable the SA to kill live tokens.
containment.notes: Disabling the SA is the documented kill for short-lived credentials.

calls.reveals: Whether caller can impersonate the SA
calls.log_notes: Data Access log; must be enabled

calls.reveals: Object names and metadata in a bucket
calls.log_notes: Listing objects is a DATA_READ Data Access audit log entry; Data Access logs are off by default and must be enabled.

detections.title: Google Cloud Service Account Disabled or Deleted
detections.detects: A service account was disabled or deleted.

detections.title: Google Cloud Service Account Modified
detections.detects: A service account was created or patched.

detections.title: GCP Permissions Granted to Create or Manage Service Account Key
detections.detects: SetIamPolicy adding Service Account Token Creator or Service Account User, which allows impersonation.

detections.title: GCP IAM serviceAccounts getAccessToken Privilege Escalation
detections.detects: A granted iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken permission check (minting a service account access token).

detections.title: GCP IAM serviceAccounts.signJwt Privilege Escalation
detections.detects: SignJwt calls with granted iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt, used to mint tokens as a service account.

detections.title: GCP IAM serviceAccounts signBlob
detections.detects: A granted iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob permission check, which can be used to get a service account token.
